# Explore structures. Design proteins.

<a id="structure-literacy"></a>

## Structural biology and structure literacy

**Level:** Beginner

Read a structure as evidence about a molecule and an experiment.

**Before you begin:** Protein sequence and molecular biology basics.

### What to understand

- Protein architecture, interactions, thermodynamics, and structure–function relationships.
- Experimental method, resolution where applicable, missing residues, and validation reports.
- Chains, biological assemblies, sequence mapping, and molecular visualization.

### What you’ll be able to do

Inspect a structure and write a short account of what it supports and what remains uncertain.

### Try this

Complete the protein-structure starter project, then locate a missing region or a validation concern in a second entry.

### Keep in mind

A deposited coordinate model is an interpretation of evidence. Check the experimental method and validation information before drawing conclusions.

### A few good resources

- [PDB-101: understanding PDB data](https://pdb101.rcsb.org/learn/guide-to-understanding-pdb-data/introduction) — Guide · Beginner · Free · English. A welcoming introduction to structure files, experimental information, assemblies, and interpretation.
  - Prerequisites: Basic protein biology.

- [RCSB PDB: learning resources](https://www.rcsb.org/) — Database · Beginner · Free · English. Find experimental structures and inspect entry-specific methods, sequence information, and validation evidence.
  - Prerequisites: Basic protein biology.

- [UCSF ChimeraX tutorials](https://www.rbvi.ucsf.edu/chimerax/tutorials.html) — Tutorial · Beginner · Tutorials free; software terms vary by use · English. Learn molecular visualization through worked examples; check the current software license for your intended use.
  - Prerequisites: Basic structural biology.

- [Biopython Tutorial and Cookbook](https://biopython.org/docs/latest/Tutorial/) — Documentation · Intermediate · Free · English. Practical biological sequence and structure handling, including parsers used in the protein-structure starter project.
  - Prerequisites: Basic Python.

<a id="prediction"></a>

## Structure prediction and confidence

**Level:** Intermediate

Understand the question a prediction answers and how to assess its reliability.

**Before you begin:** Structure literacy and sequence alignment basics.

### What to understand

- Sequence-to-structure prediction, templates, alignments, and complexes.
- Local confidence, relative-domain confidence, and model-specific quality measures.
- Sequence correspondence, experimental comparisons, and sources of uncertainty.

### What you’ll be able to do

Explain why a predicted region or interface is more or less trustworthy.

### Try this

Choose a protein with both experimental and predicted structures. Align the sequences first, inspect confidence, and document which regions are comparable.

### Keep in mind

Confidence scores are not interchangeable with experimental B-factors. A confident prediction alone does not establish binding, function, or a mechanism.

### A few good resources

- [EMBL-EBI: AlphaFold practical guide](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/alphafold/) — Course · Intermediate · Free · English. Learn access routes, interpretation, strengths, limitations, and confidence assessment for predicted structures.
  - Prerequisites: Basic protein structure knowledge.

- [Interpreting AlphaFold confidence scores](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/alphafold/inputs-and-outputs/evaluating-alphafolds-predicted-structures-using-confidence-scores/) — Guide · Intermediate · Free · English. Understand local confidence and relative-domain uncertainty before using a prediction to support a biological claim.
  - Prerequisites: Protein structure basics.

- [ColabFold](https://github.com/sokrypton/ColabFold) — Tool · Intermediate · Code free; compute access varies · English. An accessible prediction toolkit with examples and execution options. Check current compute availability before planning a run.
  - Prerequisites: Structure prediction basics and familiarity with notebooks or command-line tools.

- [PDB-101: understanding PDB data](https://pdb101.rcsb.org/learn/guide-to-understanding-pdb-data/introduction) — Guide · Beginner · Free · English. A welcoming introduction to structure files, experimental information, assemblies, and interpretation.
  - Prerequisites: Basic protein biology.

<a id="binder-design"></a>

## Protein and binder design

**Level:** Advanced

Follow a design problem from a biological objective to candidates that need experimental testing.

**Before you begin:** Structure prediction and assessment, protein interactions, and basic scripting.

### What to understand

- Target preparation, biological assembly, accessible sites, and design constraints.
- Backbone generation, sequence design, structure prediction, and candidate filtering.
- Compare diffusion-based backbone design with optimization-based pipelines such as BindCraft.
- Diversity, controls, expression and solubility considerations, and experimental validation.

### What you’ll be able to do

Describe a candidate-selection strategy and the evidence needed to test a proposed binder.

### Try this

Read one published design study and map its stages, selection metrics, controls, and experimental outcomes. Begin with published outputs before scheduling expensive generation runs.

### Keep in mind

A favorable computational score is a screening signal. Report it separately from measured affinity, specificity, and experimental success.

### A few good resources

- [RFdiffusion](https://github.com/RosettaCommons/RFdiffusion) — Tool · Advanced · Code available; GPU compute may cost · English. Explore diffusion-based protein backbone generation and conditional design through the authors' code and examples.
  - Prerequisites: Protein design, structure assessment, and command-line experience.

- [ProteinMPNN](https://github.com/dauparas/ProteinMPNN) — Tool · Advanced · Code available; compute may cost · English. Study sequence design conditioned on a protein backbone as a distinct stage in a broader design workflow.
  - Prerequisites: Protein structures, sequence design, and scripting.

- [EMBL-EBI: AlphaFold practical guide](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/alphafold/) — Course · Intermediate · Free · English. Learn access routes, interpretation, strengths, limitations, and confidence assessment for predicted structures.
  - Prerequisites: Basic protein structure knowledge.

- [BindCraft](https://github.com/martinpacesa/BindCraft) — Tool · Advanced · Code available; dependency licenses and GPU costs vary · English. An optimization-based binder-design pipeline combining AlphaFold-based design, sequence design, and filtering. Compare its strategy with diffusion-based approaches and inspect dependency terms.
  - Prerequisites: Binder design, structure assessment, and suitable GPU access.

<a id="diffusion-for-design"></a>

## Diffusion models in molecular design

**Level:** Advanced

Connect denoising and conditional generation to a biological design task.

**Before you begin:** Basic machine learning; probability and linear algebra help with the deeper material.

### What to understand

- Forward corruption, learned denoising, sampling, and conditioning.
- Representation choices, geometric constraints, and symmetry.
- Training versus inference, diversity, and evaluation beyond visually plausible structures.

### What you’ll be able to do

Explain what is generated, what conditions the generation, and how candidates are evaluated.

### Try this

Draw the sampling process for a binder-design example and identify where target information and constraints enter. Continue with the AI foundations path for the mathematics.

### Keep in mind

Learn the model's task and representation explicitly. Different diffusion systems do not share identical inputs, outputs, or validation criteria.

### A few good resources

- [RFdiffusion](https://github.com/RosettaCommons/RFdiffusion) — Tool · Advanced · Code available; GPU compute may cost · English. Explore diffusion-based protein backbone generation and conditional design through the authors' code and examples.
  - Prerequisites: Protein design, structure assessment, and command-line experience.

- [Dive into Deep Learning](https://d2l.ai/) — Book · Intermediate · Free online · English. Build conceptual and practical foundations in deep learning; select chapters relevant to the model you are studying.
  - Prerequisites: Python, probability, linear algebra, and basic calculus for deeper chapters.

<a id="simulation"></a>

## Molecular simulation and biophysics

**Level:** Advanced

Explore molecular motion through models with explicit physical assumptions.

**Before you begin:** Thermodynamics, structural biology, and command-line basics.

### What to understand

- Force fields, parameterization, solvation, and boundary conditions.
- Minimization, equilibration, sampling, replicates, and convergence.
- Trajectory analysis and the relationship between observables and a biological question.

### What you’ll be able to do

Explain the assumptions and sampling limitations of a simulation study.

### Try this

Follow an introductory simulation example and record the force field, ensemble, integration settings, and analysis choices.

### Keep in mind

A stable-looking trajectory alone does not demonstrate convergence or establish a biological mechanism.

### A few good resources

- [OpenMM user guide](https://docs.openmm.org/latest/userguide/) — Documentation · Advanced · Free; compute may cost · English. Learn simulation setup, execution, and analysis with explicit attention to the physical model and settings.
  - Prerequisites: Molecular simulation basics and Python.

- [GROMACS documentation](https://manual.gromacs.org/current/) — Documentation · Advanced · Free; compute may cost · English. A reference for molecular dynamics methods, file formats, commands, and reproducible simulation configuration.
  - Prerequisites: Thermodynamics, molecular structures, and command-line use.
